speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are starting a new term of Government under the shadow of COVID-19.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Many cities that had initially suppressed the virus are seeing infections rise again as they reopen their economies.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Scientists are still learning new things about the virus – including how best to protect ourselves and how new medical treatments and vaccines can help.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must therefore adjust our COVID-19 strategies and plans along the way.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We have prepared our healthcare system and expanded reserve capacity to deal with a possible resurgence of cases.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are continuing to ramp up our ability to conduct aggressive testing and contact tracing.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Most importantly, all of us must stay vigilant to prevent a new wave of infections.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: At the same time, we are facing our worst recession since Independence.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These measures have reduced the immediate pain, but things will remain grave for quite some time.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The situations globally and domestically have changed and there is no going back to the status quo ante.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: For decades, Singapore has thrived under globalisation and a stable international order.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But our external environment has become less benign and predictable.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: It has revealed new threats, while also opening up fresh opportunities.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Global fault lines have sharpened, and US-China rivalry has intensified.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Countries are fighting to meet their own needs, fuelling a new wave of protectionism.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This is especially challenging for Singapore, as we make our living by doing business with the world.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Domestically, Singapore is at an inflection point of our history.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: New generations of Singaporeans are coming of age.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We have new aspirations and expectations, including a desire for more diverse voices to be heard, and stronger checks and balances.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: At the same time, new leaders are emerging to take Singapore the next steps forward.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The new generation of leaders and Singaporeans will have to form bonds and connections afresh, forge their own compact, find their own ways of working together and strike their own balances.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: They have to continue to deliver effective and sound government, while accommodating the growing diversity of views.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: And they have to foster a more open spirit in our society, even as we strengthen the common cause holding us together as Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: For Singapore to continue to succeed, we need to understand these changes in our external and domestic environments, rethink our problems and improve on the status quo.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The Government will continue to evolve our economic and social models, and our policies to suit the new circumstances.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will listen to and examine novel ideas objectively, recognising that no solutions are right for all time.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Sometimes, staying the course will remain the best way forward and we must convince Singaporeans to persevere.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Other problems will require fresh approaches and the courage to take a different direction.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In all cases, we will seek to do what is best for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Despite the sea change in our environment, one thing remains constant: Singapore is still a little red dot in an uncertain world.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: To survive and thrive, we must stand out compared to other countries.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We need to be more resilient and nimble than others in responding to change.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must do things that others cannot do, and do the things that others can do, even better.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This requires us to reach a broad consensus on the economic and social changes necessary, the Singaporean identity we aspire to forge, and the kind of politics we want to have.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We recognise the fears and anxieties about jobs that Singaporeans have today.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: COVID-19 has amplified the pressures caused by a slowing global economy in recent years, especially on certain groups of workers, such as our lower wage workers, mature workers and mid-career Singaporeans with heavier financial commitments and families to support.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Keeping people in work is the best way to help them take care of their families and to keep their skills current until the economy improves.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are doing all we can to help.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are supporting businesses, especially SMEs, with cashflow and credit so that they stay afloat and hold on to their workers.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: I urge employers to see mid-career Singaporeans as valuable assets, and provide them with opportunities and training for new jobs.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: To sustain job creation, we must keep our economy strong and competitive.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Some sectors will not return to what they were before.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Much of our economy thrives because we have made ourselves a vibrant hub for the region and an attractive place for trade, investments, talent and ideas.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We cannot take our hub status for granted, or assume that its scope and role will remain the same.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Our efforts to fortify our resilience in critical areas like food, healthcare and supply chain management can become new sources of growth.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will also make a major push for sustainable growth.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: With creativity and resourcefulness, we can turn our aspirations for a greener Singapore into a competitive advantage.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: While we pursue economic growth to create opportunities for Singaporeans, we must also share the benefits of progress widely with all citizens.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We started strengthening our social safety nets more than a decade ago.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In this crisis, we have implemented many emergency measures to help Singaporeans cope.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These are temporary relief measures, but we do expect a permanent shift to a new normal after the crisis.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are entering an era of volatility, uncertainty and disruption in people’s lives.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Individuals will need greater social support than before.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will have to consider carefully how to strengthen our safety nets, to give Singaporeans more assurance coping with life’s uncertainties.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: And we will have to be careful to do so in a way that is financially sustainable for future generations.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will support young families to own their homes, and to improve their own and their children’s lives through quality education and training pathways.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will offer middle-aged Singaporeans more help to secure good jobs and greater assurance of retirement adequacy.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We will take good care of our seniors to enable them to age well and with dignity.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But more redistribution cannot be the only way to level up those who are doing less well.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We also have to continue strengthening social mobility and broadening our conception of merit.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Meritocracy has been a crucial pillar of our society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: It has served us well over the past 55 years.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: However, just as our social norms and policies have evolved in tandem with Singapore’s development, so too must our model of meritocracy.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We recognise that unfettered meritocracy can foster excessive competition.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We also realise the need to level up families who are at a disadvantage, and give their children a fair start in life.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We want to keep our society open and socially mobile, and not allow it to stratify and ossify over time.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: That is why we have made a concerted effort to value a wide range of talents.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Schools and Institutes of Higher Learning admit students through yardsticks other than academic results.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The Public Service Commission has widened its catchment of scholars.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Employers are encouraged to hire people based on skills, with the public service taking the lead.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Political parties are fielding candidates who took different life paths and have diverse talents and strengths.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: This is also why we must continue to invest heavily in education and training, from the earliest years of childhood through the schooling years.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Employers must support lifelong learning as the new norm.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Society must value people for what they contribute, in every job and every role.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Building a fair and just society goes beyond Government actions.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We have made progress over the last decade, and we will do much more in this term of Government to see our people through this crisis and beyond.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The more closely knit we are as a people, the further we can move ahead as a nation.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In the longer term, the key to Singapore’s success lies in our sense of shared identity.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Singapore can endure and secure her place in history, only if Singaporeans feel passionately about our country, and put our hearts and souls into making this a better home.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Since Independence, we have gradually built a distinctive Singaporean culture and identity.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Regardless of race, language or religion, we all think of ourselves as Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: You can see this in our attitudes, memories and experiences; it is in our arts and heritage, and the way we cheer for Team Singapore together.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: You see it in the way we can gladly identify one another in an unfamiliar foreign land, and the way we have each other’s backs in a crisis.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These are emotional ties that are strengthened over the years.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: There is still much more to do to strengthen the sense of togetherness in our society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must start young and shape the multi-cultural instincts in our children early in life; our approaches and methods must therefore evolve with the outlook and attitudes of the young.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must then sustain this mindset across our communities and workplaces.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must also recognise that larger forces are at play that test our solidarity and pull us in different directions.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The social media has amplified contending voices and views.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We are more exposed than ever to causes, attitudes and values from other societies that may not be relevant to our social context, but will influence us nonetheless.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Economic distress arising from COVID-19, or social inequality, can breed a sense of insecurity amongst different groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Multiracialism will always be a core element of our Singaporean identity.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Everyone, regardless of race, language or religion, must have an equal place in our society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Here in Singapore, we embrace our plurality and diversity, even as we continue to develop a stronger Singaporean ethos and strive together to become more than the sum of our individual parts.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But our multiracialism is still work in progress.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Each successive generation will bring different life experiences and perspectives.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In each generation, some will want to discuss sensitive issues afresh.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Younger Singaporeans prefer talking about these issues more candidly and openly, which is a positive development.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But the conversation needs to be conducted with restraint and mutual respect, because race, language and religion will always be visceral subjects.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: If each group pushes its own agenda to the extreme, we risk eroding the common space and fracturing our social cohesion.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: They not only touch on matters of livelihood, but also on our sense of identity and belonging.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: As masters of our own land, Singaporeans must have confidence in the rights and privileges of citizenship.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: At the same time, we must not turn inwards, away from the world.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must keep our hearts open to those who come from beyond our shores.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We should continue to welcome and integrate those who can contribute to Singapore, and improve our lives and our children’s future.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Our Singaporean identity has been formed and strengthened not by excluding those who arrive later, but by successive arrivals adding to the richness of our society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These are emotive issues that can evoke strong reactions.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Debates on such sensitive matters can easily become polarised.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: So, as we open up more areas for meaningful discussion, Singaporeans must work even harder to listen to and understand one another.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must break out of the echo chambers that form so easily online, and make genuine attempts to bridge the gap with those who think differently from us.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must strive to obtain greater insight, build shared understanding and use our diverse perspectives and ideas to achieve better outcomes for all.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: These must also be the guiding principles of our politics.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Parliament is the central platform to debate national policies and set the tone for our political discourse.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The Government and the Opposition both have roles to play to build trust in our public institutions and achieve good outcomes for Singapore.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Given the magnitude of the challenges and uncertainties, we must expect to encounter more differences in views and interests among Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must learn to handle these differences constructively.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: On some issues, we can agree to disagree.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But on issues core to Singapore’s survival and future, we must do our best to find common ground and build a broad consensus.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The Government will be open to constructive criticism and rational debate, and to new ways of doing things.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But the Government, having been elected by the people, must also govern for all our people.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: It cannot shy away from taking difficult and tough decisions in the national interest, or shirk the duty of winning support for such decisions.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The Opposition too has its part to play.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: And when the situation demands, both the Government and Opposition should set aside differences and work together to secure the safety and future of our nation.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Singaporeans’ expectations and choices will determine what kind of politics Singapore will have.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: The key question is how to forge a common cause together, regardless of our own political inclinations.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We need to base our rhetoric on a responsible sense of the realities and come to a shared understanding about our goals and constraints.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Our public debates should be honest and open about the trade-offs of different options and what they will cost society.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Singaporeans aspire to make this a better place and have interesting and diverse ideas to pursue.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Such a diversity of views and ideas can be a source of strength, for us to navigate the challenges and possibilities ahead.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: Singaporeans must come together, in partnership, to pursue the greater good, united by a belief in Singapore and a desire to turn our vision into reality.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We invite all Singaporeans to partner each other and the Government in this journey.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: In the coming years, we will confront major changes in the world.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: But we can face the future with confidence, having built up deep strengths since our Independence.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: We must continue to command confidence and respect in the world, and emerge a stronger and more united nation.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: So, let us work in close partnership, as Singapore Together – one people uniting behind our elected Government – to save lives, protect livelihoods and secure a brighter future for ourselves and our children.

speaker: The President (Mdm Halimah Yacob)
text: ADDENDA TO THE PRESIDENT'S ADDRESS AT THE OPENING OF THE FIRST SESSION OF THE FOURTEENTH PARLIAMENT ON MONDAY, 24 AUGUST 2020
